tests.title: Main classes and test compile warning-free with JDK only, and the harness exits 0
tests.target: javac --release 25 -Xlint:all -Werror -d "$OUT" on Customer.java, SalesOrderLine.java, SalesOrder.java and src/test/java/com/neversoft/sales/SalesOrderTest.java, then java -cp "$OUT" com.neversoft.sales.SalesOrderTest
tests.rationale: AC-6 is a property of the compiler run itself (no classpath, -Werror) and can't be proved by a test inside the code under compilation. It is also the critical path: if it passes, the feature is alive and every other test in the harness ran.

tests.title: Only new files are added, no existing file is modified
tests.target: git status --porcelain and git diff --name-only <base>...HEAD: only added files under src/main/java/com/neversoft/{sales,customer}, src/test/java/com/neversoft/sales and docs/bob/4; Vehicle.java, VehicleTest.java and package.json unchanged
tests.rationale: AC-7 is about repository state, not runtime behaviour. Only a VCS check can prove it.

tests.title: Associate a customer and add lines to an order
tests.gherkin:
Given a Customer "Acme Ltd"
  And two SalesOrderLines with item codes "A-1" and "B-2"
  And a new SalesOrder with an id, an order date and status "NEW"
When the customer is set on the order
  And both lines are added with addLine in order
Then getCustomer() returns that customer
  And getLines() contains exactly the two lines in insertion order
  And getId(), getOrderDate() and getStatus() return the values supplied
tests.rationale: The main user story from the issue (an order with child lines related to a customer). It spans the three classes as a caller would use them.

tests.title: Remove a line from an order
tests.gherkin:
Given a SalesOrder holding two lines
When removeLine is called with one of those lines
Then it returns true
  And the order holds exactly one line, the other one
When removeLine is called with a line that is not in the order
Then it returns false
  And the order still holds one line
tests.rationale: AC-4 says 'manage' the collection. Remove is the caller-visible half of that scenario and complements T-3.

tests.title: Build all three classes with their all-fields constructors
tests.gherkin:
Given distinct values for every field of Customer, SalesOrderLine and SalesOrder
When each object is created with its all-fields constructor
Then every getter on all three classes returns the value that was passed in
  And the SalesOrder holds the supplied customer and lines
tests.rationale: A caller-facing scenario that proves the three field sets named in AC-1, AC-2 and AC-3 and the parameterised constructors end to end.

tests.title: Equal object graphs are equal; one change anywhere breaks equality
tests.rationale: SalesOrder.equals and hashCode delegate to Customer and SalesOrderLine. That delegation is the boundary between the classes and can't be seen from a single class's unit test. Two identical graphs are equal with equal hashCode; changing one field in the customer, a line, the line order or the line count makes them unequal.

tests.title: toString and hashCode on a full graph terminate and include nested data
tests.rationale: The risk is recursion across the parent and child classes, which only shows when the full graph is exercised. toString of a populated order returns normally and contains the customer name and each line's item code; hashCode returns normally.
traces_to: risk: Circular reference between SalesOrder and SalesOrderLine in toString/hashCode/equals

tests.title: Customer structure
tests.rationale: Pure structural facts about one class, same technique as VehicleTest T-7 and T-8: public, extends Object, no interfaces, exactly 4 private non-static fields (long id, String name, String email, String phone), public no-arg and 4-arg constructors, getter and setter per field.

tests.title: SalesOrderLine structure, with no back-reference to SalesOrder
tests.rationale: Structural facts about one class: public, exactly 6 private non-static fields (long id, String itemCode, String description, int quantity, BigDecimal unitPrice, BigDecimal lineAmount), public no-arg and 6-arg constructors, getter and setter per field. The 'no SalesOrder field' assertion is a cheap, deterministic guard on the recursion risk.
traces_to: risk: Circular reference between SalesOrder and SalesOrderLine in toString/hashCode/equals

tests.title: SalesOrder structure
tests.rationale: Structural facts about one class: public, exactly 5 private non-static fields (long id, LocalDate orderDate, String status, Customer customer, List<SalesOrderLine> lines), public no-arg and 5-arg constructors, and getLines, setLines, addLine, removeLine (boolean), getCustomer and setCustomer with the specified signatures.

tests.title: Classes are in the conventional packages
tests.rationale: A class-loading check needs no collaborators. Class.forName succeeds for com.neversoft.customer.Customer, com.neversoft.sales.SalesOrderLine and com.neversoft.sales.SalesOrder, fixing the package paths future modules would depend on.
traces_to: risk: Package naming conflicts with future modularization

tests.title: No-arg constructor defaults
tests.rationale: Pure constructor logic per class: numeric fields are 0, reference fields are null, and SalesOrder.getLines() is empty and non-null.

tests.title: Setter and getter round trip per field
tests.rationale: Simple accessor logic with no collaborators. For every field the getter returns what the setter stored, including null for reference fields. lineAmount stores whatever is set and is not derived from quantity x unit price.

tests.title: equals contract
tests.rationale: Pure method logic per class: reflexive, symmetric, false for null and for another type, true for a separately constructed instance with the same field values.

tests.title: equals is false when any single field differs
tests.rationale: Covers the per-field branches in equals. Each branch is only reachable by varying one field at a time: Customer (4 fields), SalesOrderLine (6) and SalesOrder (5).

tests.title: hashCode is consistent with equals
tests.rationale: Pure method logic per class: equal instances have equal hash codes, hashCode is stable across calls, and at least one pair differing in a field hashes differently (sanity check, not a collision guarantee).

tests.title: Null-safe equals, hashCode and toString on default instances
tests.rationale: Covers the null branches of Objects.equals and Objects.hash. Default (all-null) instances of all three classes, and a SalesOrder with a null customer, don't throw; two default instances are equal.

tests.title: toString contains every field value and the specified shape
tests.rationale: Pure string-building logic per class: starts with the simple class name and contains each field name and value. SalesOrder.toString shows customer= and lines=; SalesOrderLine.toString shows no order reference.
traces_to: risk: Circular reference between SalesOrder and SalesOrderLine in toString/hashCode/equals

tests.title: getLines returns an unmodifiable view
tests.rationale: Encapsulation logic inside SalesOrder. add and remove on the getLines() result throw UnsupportedOperationException and leave the order unchanged; the view reflects a later addLine.

tests.title: addLine rejects null
tests.rationale: A single guard branch in SalesOrder: addLine(null) throws NullPointerException and the lines list is unchanged.

tests.title: setLines and the all-fields constructor take a defensive copy
tests.rationale: Aliasing logic inside SalesOrder. Mutating the caller's list after setLines or the 5-arg constructor doesn't change the order's lines, and setLines replaces the previous contents instead of appending.

tests.title: Lines are never null
tests.rationale: Covers the null branch in setLines and the field initialiser: the no-arg constructor, setLines(null) and the all-fields constructor with null lines all give an empty, non-null list, and addLine works straight after construction.

tests.title: setCustomer replaces and clears the association
tests.rationale: The customer association method (AC-4) is a single setter on SalesOrder. setCustomer(c1) then setCustomer(c2) leaves c2, setCustomer(null) clears it, and later changes to the Customer are visible through getCustomer() because it is held by reference.

tests.title: removeLine semantics
tests.rationale: Covers branches of List.remove as used by SalesOrder; the caller-level view is T-4. Matches by equals, removes only the first of two equal lines, returns true on removal and false for an absent line, null or an empty order, and keeps the relative order of the remaining lines.

tests.title: BigDecimal scale sensitivity is the documented behaviour
tests.rationale: Pins the low-level plan's design decision so a later change is deliberate, and needs no collaborators. SalesOrderLines with unitPrice 1.0 vs 1.00 are not equal; lines with the same value and scale are equal with equal hash codes.

gaps: Risk 'Domain field requirements evolve as business logic is added': not tested. It is a future-change risk mitigated by design (simple POJOs). The structural tests T-8, T-9 and T-10 assert exact field counts and will fail on purpose when fields change, forcing a conscious update.
Wiring into npm test / CI is not tested. The low-level plan keeps package.json unchanged (AC-7), so the harness is run only through the Javadoc commands (T-1).
Thread-safety, serialization and persistence are not tested. They are out of scope for the plain POJOs in this issue.
The semantics of status values (a free String, no enum) and of lineAmount (stored, not computed) are only pinned by T-13. No business rules exist to test.
